title: Form controls rendered by OSelect / OInput have no programmatic label
wcag_criteria: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions; 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
component_source: web/src/lib/forms/Select/OSelect.vue (:136-140, :1199), web/src/lib/forms/Input/OInput.vue (:16-25, :274, :298-302); call sites that render a visible label outside the component (e.g. alert create form)
selector: button[role=combobox][data-test$=-trigger] without label; input[type=number] in alert settings (e.g. [data-test=alert-trigger-threshold-input-field])
evidence: test-results/interact-results.json#alertAdd.labels; screenshots/states/ix-alert-add.png; axe rules label (21 nodes / 12 pages) and button-name on combobox triggers
repro_steps: 1. Open /web/alerts/add. 2. Inspect "Stream Type", "Stream Name", "Alert if", "Critical if", "Check every", "Look back window", "Cooldown period", "Hold for", destinations. 3. Each control has no <label for>, aria-label or aria-labelledby (14 of 14 controls sampled).
expected: Each control exposes the visible label text as its accessible name.
actual: Visible labels are separate text nodes; controls are announced as "combobox, collapsed" / "spin button" with no name. Passing aria-label to OSelect/OInput lands on the wrapper div (inheritAttrs:false + v-bind="$attrs" on the root), not the control.
user_impact: Screen-reader and voice-control users cannot tell which field they are editing; creating an alert (core workflow) is effectively blocked without sight.
root_cause: OSelect/OInput forward $attrs to the wrapper; 171 of 321 OSelect usages pass no `label` prop; OInput labelPosition="inside" renders a <span> not a <label>.
recommended_fix: In OSelect/OInput/OSwitch forward aria-* attrs to the focusable control (split $attrs: class/style to wrapper, rest to control). Require `label` or `ariaLabel` prop (dev-time warning when neither). Update call sites to pass the visible label via `label` or `aria-labelledby`.
example_code:
<!-- OSelect.vue -->
<button role="combobox" :id="triggerId" :aria-labelledby="label ? labelId : undefined" :aria-label="!label ? ariaLabel : undefined" v-bind="controlAttrs">
retest: Run axe on /alerts/add, /alerts/anomaly/add, /ai/experiments/new, /settings/general and the logs date picker; expect 0 label / combobox button-name violations; confirm names in Chrome accessibility tree.

title: Monaco query editor traps Tab; only escape is an undocumented shortcut, and its focus border is removed
component_source: web/src/components/CodeQueryEditor.vue (:531 editor creation, :1291-1299 focus border removed)
repro_steps: 1. Open /web/logs. 2. Tab to the query editor. 3. Press Tab, Shift+Tab, Escape, Ctrl+M: focus stays in "Editor content" (7 consecutive Tab presses). 4. Ctrl+Shift+M (macOS) toggles tab-focus mode and Tab then leaves the editor.
expected: Tab moves focus out of the editor, or the exit method is announced/visible (2.1.2 requires the user be advised when a non-standard key is needed).
actual: Tab inserts indentation; exit requires Ctrl+Shift+M / Ctrl+M which nothing in the UI documents; the focused editor shows no focus ring.
user_impact: Keyboard-only users get stuck in the primary log search box, the most-used surface of the product.
root_cause: Monaco defaults (tabFocusMode off); no `accessibilitySupport`/`tabFocusMode` option; CSS sets --vscode-focusBorder: transparent.
recommended_fix: Enable tabFocusMode for single-line/short query editors (or bind Escape to leave the editor), add a visible hint ("Press Esc then Tab to move focus") via aria-describedby, and restore a :focus-within ring on the editor container.
example_code:
monaco.editor.create(el, { ...opts, tabFocusMode: true, ariaLabel: t('search.queryEditor') });
// CSS: .query-editor:focus-within { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-focus-ring); }
retest: Keyboard-only: Tab into and out of the editor on /logs, /metrics, /traces, /alerts/add (SQL mode), /pipeline/functions; confirm visible focus ring.
confidence: High (macOS Chromium tested; Windows shortcut not tested)
scope_note: All Monaco instances (logs, metrics, traces, alert SQL, functions, pipelines) share CodeQueryEditor.vue - only /logs exercised.

title: Login: "Login as internal user" is not reachable or operable by keyboard
evidence: test-results/public-results.json (internalFormOpenedByKeyboard=false; tab walk skips the link); screenshots/states/public-login-sso-choice.png
repro_steps: 1. Sign out, open /web/login (SSO enabled). 2. Press Tab repeatedly: focus goes SSO button -> body, never the link. 3. Focus it programmatically and press Enter: nothing happens.
expected: Link/button is in the Tab order and opens the email/password form on Enter/Space.
actual: <a> without href is not focusable and has no key handler.
user_impact: Keyboard-only and switch users with internal (non-SSO) accounts cannot sign in at all.
root_cause: Anchor used as a button without href/role/tabindex.
recommended_fix: Replace with <OButton variant="link" type="button" :aria-expanded="loginAsInternalUser" aria-controls="internal-login-form">.
retest: Keyboard-only login with an internal test account; axe on /login.

title: Shared table pagination: first/prev/next/last buttons and rows-per-page select have no accessible name
repro_steps: Open any OTable list (e.g. /web/streams); inspect the pagination buttons: icon-only OButtons with no aria-label; page-size select has visible "Records per page" text not associated.
expected: Buttons named "First page", "Previous page", "Next page", "Last page"; select named "Records per page".
actual: Announced as "button" x4 and an unnamed combobox.
user_impact: Screen-reader users cannot page through any list in the product (54 routes).
root_cause: Icon-only OButton without aria-label; OSelect label not wired.
recommended_fix: Add translated aria-labels in OTablePagination.vue; give the page-size OSelect `:aria-label="t('search.recordsPerPage')"` (after A11Y-01 fix) and wrap the pager in <nav aria-label="Pagination">.
retest: axe on /streams, /alerts, /dashboards, /iam/users: no button-name on o2-table-* selectors.

title: Icon-only buttons across feature pages have no accessible name (tooltip-only labelling)
wcag_criteria: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 2.5.3 Label in Name
component_source: OButton (web/src/lib/core/Button/OButton.vue:425-466) + OTooltip child pattern (web/src/lib/overlay/Tooltip/OTooltip.vue:161-237, 350-355); ~406 icon-only call sites (source scan)
evidence: test-results/rule-signatures.json; test-results/kb-results.json#tab_logs; test-results/final-results.json#dashboardView.axe (17 unnamed on dashboard view)
repro_steps: Open /web/logs and Tab through the search toolbar: histogram, more-options, refresh-cache, refresh-interval and full-screen buttons expose no name. Same on dashboard view toolbar (17 buttons).
expected: Every icon-only button has an aria-label matching its tooltip text.
actual: Tooltip text is rendered in a separate aria-hidden trigger and never names the button.
user_impact: Screen-reader and voice-control users cannot identify core actions (run histogram, refresh, export, full screen, copy code).
root_cause: OButton has no ariaLabel prop or icon-only guard; OTooltip does not set aria-describedby/aria-label on its trigger.
recommended_fix: Make OTooltip label its trigger (aria-label when trigger has no text, aria-describedby otherwise); add an `ariaLabel` prop to OButton and a dev warning / lint rule for icon-only buttons without one; add vue-flow Controls aria-labels.
example_code:
// OButton.vue (dev only)
if (import.meta.env.DEV && isIconOnly.value && !attrs["aria-label"] && !attrs["aria-labelledby"]) console.warn("[OButton] icon-only button needs aria-label");
retest: axe button-name across the crawl list should drop from 709 nodes to only intentional exceptions.

title: Theme accent colour fails text contrast (primary buttons, links, active tabs/folders)
component_source: web/src/utils/theme.ts:136-149 (pickButtonForeground accepts white at >= 3:1), web/src/constants/themes.ts:72-80 (O2 Signature #6B76E3, active on this org)
selector: .o-tab__label (active tab), [data-test=o-truncated-text] in active tab/folder, primary OButton labels, .text-text-link / .text-accent links
repro_steps: With org theme "O2 Signature" (light), open any page with an active tab or primary button (e.g. /web/streams "New stream", /web/alerts tabs) and measure contrast.
expected: >= 4.5:1 for normal-size text.
actual: 3.3-3.94:1. Code comment explicitly accepts 3:1 for white-on-accent.
user_impact: Low-vision users struggle to read the most important calls to action and the current-location indicator on almost every page (136 routes).
root_cause: Brand accent used directly as text/background colour; contrast floor set to 3:1 by design.
recommended_fix: Derive accessible text/background shades from each theme colour (e.g. darken accent to >= 4.5:1 against white and against its tint for text; use 4.5:1 floor in pickButtonForeground). Add a contrast unit test over PREDEFINED_THEMES and validate custom org themes on save.
retest: axe color-contrast on the crawl list with each predefined theme in light and dark.
confidence: High (measured with O2 Signature theme; other themes not measured)

title: Low-contrast secondary text: placeholders, muted values, syntax colours, meta labels
component_source: Design tokens text-select-placeholder (#a3a3a3), text-text-muted (#d4d4d4 in some views), text-text-placeholder, highlight.js theme in ingestion code blocks, dbm tab meta
repro_steps: Open /web/alerts/add (placeholder "Alert name"), /web/home Usage values, /web/ingestion/servers/nginx code blocks; measure contrast.
expected: >= 4.5:1 (placeholder text that conveys information counts).
user_impact: Low-vision users cannot read hints, current usage numbers and code samples.
root_cause: Grey/semantic tokens tuned for aesthetics not contrast.
recommended_fix: Raise placeholder/muted tokens to >= #737373 on white (4.7:1); switch highlight.js light theme to a WCAG-AA palette; avoid opacity-reduced text (opacity-55/80).
retest: axe color-contrast on /alerts/add, /home (Usage tab), /ingestion/*, /infra/databases.

title: Images without text alternative (AI assistant icon on 134 routes, SSO icon, custom logos)
repro_steps: Open any page; inspect the AI gradient icon image: no alt attribute.
expected: Decorative images have alt="" ; meaningful ones a short alt.
actual: No alt; screen readers may read the file name.
user_impact: Noise ("ai_icon_gradient.svg") for screen-reader users on nearly every page.
root_cause: Missing alt attribute.
recommended_fix: Add alt="" (decorative, the parent button carries the name) or a translated alt where the image is the only content.
retest: axe image-alt across crawl list = 0.

title: Table row / header selection checkboxes have no accessible name
repro_steps: Open /web/streams; Tab to a row checkbox: announced "checkbox, not checked" with no name.
expected: "Select row <name>" / "Select all rows".
actual: No name.
user_impact: Bulk actions (delete, move) are unusable non-visually.
root_cause: OCheckbox rendered without ariaLabel.
recommended_fix: Pass `:aria-label` built from the row label (or "Select all rows" in header).
retest: axe on /streams, /dashboards, /alerts, /iam/users.

title: Charts (ECharts canvas) have no text alternative; every panel reuses id="chart1"
evidence: test-results/final-results.json#dashboardView (5 canvases, host=none, duplicate id chart1 x5); screenshots/states/dashboard-view.png
repro_steps: Open any dashboard (/web/dashboards -> first row). Inspect panels: <canvas> inside div#chart1 with no role/aria-label; ids repeat.
expected: Each chart has role="img" + aria-label summarising title/series, and a keyboard-reachable data-table alternative.
actual: Canvas only; no name, no data alternative.
user_impact: Blind users get nothing from dashboards, metrics, RUM, infra and usage charts.
root_cause: ECharts aria option not enabled; no fallback table.
recommended_fix: Register AriaComponent and set `aria: { enabled: true, decal: { show: true } }` (decal also helps 1.4.1); wrap chart in role="img" with aria-label of panel title; offer "View as table" per panel; use unique ids.
example_code:
import { AriaComponent } from 'echarts/components'; use([AriaComponent]);
option.aria = { enabled: true, decal: { show: true } };
retest: Inspect dashboard panels in accessibility tree; VoiceOver reads chart description.
scope_note: Confirmed on dashboard view; other chart pages share ChartRenderer (inferred).

title: No "skip to main content" mechanism
evidence: test-results/kb-results.json (first 10 Tab stops on every page are header controls); shell probe skipLink=0
repro_steps: Load /web/logs; press Tab: 9 header controls + sidebar precede page content on every page.
expected: First Tab stop is a "Skip to main content" link targeting <main>.
actual: None. Landmarks exist (header/nav/main) which partially mitigate for screen-reader users only.
user_impact: Keyboard users press Tab ~10 times on every page load before reaching content.
root_cause: Not implemented.
recommended_fix: Add a visually-hidden-until-focused skip link as the first child of the layout pointing to <main id="main-content" tabindex="-1">.
retest: Tab once on any page -> skip link visible; Enter moves focus into main.

title: Dropdown triggers put ARIA/button attributes on a non-interactive wrapper div
component_source: web/src/lib/overlay/Dropdown/ODropdown.vue:288 (DropdownMenuTrigger as-child on a <div class="relative inline-flex"> slot)
repro_steps: Open /web/alerts; inspect the "More" / split-button dropdown triggers: div carries type, disabled, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded; the real button inside has no expanded state.
expected: aria-haspopup/aria-expanded on the focusable button.
actual: On a wrapper div; menu open state not announced.
user_impact: Screen-reader users are not told a control opens a menu or whether it is open.
root_cause: Callers pass a wrapper element into the trigger slot.
recommended_fix: Pass the OButton itself as the trigger slot root, or have ODropdown render its own OButton trigger.
retest: axe aria-allowed-attr = 0; trigger announces "menu button, collapsed".

title: Toast notifications: double announcements, short life, invalid list markup, focusable aria-hidden sentinels
component_source: web/src/lib/feedback/Toast/OToast.vue (:102-104, :152-158), useToast.ts:29-34, toast viewport in web/src/App.vue:20
evidence: test-results/final-results.json#toast (message text rendered in role=alert span AND role=status li; disappeared ~2 s after activation); rule-signatures list/aria-hidden-focus (10-12 pages)
repro_steps: 1. /web/logs -> open date picker -> "Copy time range". 2. Observe live regions: "Notification Date range copiedDate range copied" in assertive alert plus status li. 3. Toast gone ~2 s later. 4. Error toast on login/alert save shows the same duplication.
expected: One polite announcement for success, assertive only for errors; toast persists >= 5 s and pauses on focus as well as hover; valid list markup.
actual: Message announced twice (once assertively for a success); auto-dismiss ~2 s for this toast; pause on hover only; ol contains non-li children and focusable aria-hidden spans.
user_impact: Repeated/interrupting speech; users with cognitive or motor disabilities may miss messages.
root_cause: Reka toast + custom aria-live wrapper both announce; timeout set per call.
recommended_fix: Use a single live region (reka built-in), role=status for success/info; minimum 5 s and pause on focus-within; keep focus sentinels outside the <ol>.
retest: VoiceOver: trigger copy + failed save, each message spoken once; timer pauses on focus.

title: Focus is lost to <body> after a failed dialog submit
repro_steps: 1. /web/dashboards -> New dashboard. 2. Leave name empty, activate Save. 3. document.activeElement is <body>.
expected: Focus moves to the first invalid field (as /alerts/add already does).
actual: Focus drops to body (error text itself is role=alert and aria-invalid is set - good).
user_impact: Keyboard users must restart navigation; screen-reader users lose context.
root_cause: Primary button disabled/re-rendered during validation, losing focus.
recommended_fix: On submit failure focus the first [aria-invalid=true] inside the dialog; avoid disabling the focused button while validating.
retest: Repeat on New dashboard, Add Folder, New stream, Add user.

title: Home: AI chat composer has no accessible name or visible focus, and receives autofocus at the end of the page
wcag_criteria: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 2.4.7 Focus Visible; 2.4.3 Focus Order
component_source: Home O2 Assistant composer (contenteditable DIV), chat history search input
selector: div[contenteditable=true] (placeholder "Show me errors from the last hour..."), input[aria-label=Search]
repro_steps: 1. Load /web/. 2. Focus starts in the composer at the bottom; Tab moves to an unnamed image-upload button, then to <body>, then wraps to the header. 3. Composer has no aria-label/labelledby; focusing it produces no visual change.
expected: Composer named ("Ask O2 Assistant"), visible focus, and initial focus on the page heading or first logical element.
actual: Unnamed textbox, no visible focus change, autofocus skips page content; image-upload button unnamed.
user_impact: Screen-reader users land on an unnamed field; keyboard users start at the end of the tab order.
root_cause: Contenteditable editor without role/label; autofocus on mount; focus styles removed (RichTextInput.vue:22 outline-none).
recommended_fix: role="textbox" aria-multiline="true" aria-label; add focus-visible ring; drop autofocus on route entry (or focus the h1).
retest: Tab order on /; axe; pixel-diff focus test.

title: Mobile navigation drawer: generic name, unnamed close button, Tab stuck on "Home", toggle lacks state
repro_steps: 1. Viewport 375x740, open /web/. 2. Enter on "Main navigation". 3. Drawer dialog is named "Drawer"; close button has no name; 19 consecutive Tab presses stay on "Home". 4. Toggle never sets aria-expanded.
expected: Drawer named "Main navigation", named close button, Tab moves through nav items, toggle exposes aria-expanded.
actual: As described; Escape closes and returns focus (good); arrow keys still move between items.
user_impact: Mobile/zoomed keyboard users (including 400% zoom users) cannot discover the rest of the navigation with Tab.
root_cause: ODrawer title fallback; ONavbar Tab-region handler has no next region inside drawer.
recommended_fix: Pass title, aria-label on close button, aria-expanded/aria-controls on toggle; let Tab leave the rail when no next region exists.
retest: Repeat at 375 px and at 400% zoom on desktop.

title: Date-time picker: unnamed popover dialog, unlabelled custom value input, Escape ignored inside relative panel
wcag_criteria: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions; 2.1.1 Keyboard
component_source: Date-time picker (data-test=date-time-*) used on logs, traces, metrics, dashboards
repro_steps: 1. /web/logs, focus "Past 15 Minutes", Enter. 2. Popover role=dialog has no aria-label/labelledby. 3. Tab into relative panel (4 Tabs) and press Escape: picker stays open.
expected: Dialog named "Select time range"; number input labelled; Escape closes from anywhere and returns focus.
actual: Escape closes only when focus is on the Relative/Absolute tabs.
user_impact: Time range is set on every query; screen-reader users get an unnamed dialog and unlabeled field.
root_cause: Search/number inputs stop Escape propagation; no title on popover.
recommended_fix: aria-label on popover content; label the number input; handle Escape at popover root.
retest: Keyboard test from each focus position in the picker.

title: Login page: no autocomplete tokens, no heading/landmark, fields not tied to server error
wcag_criteria: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose; 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; 2.4.6 Headings and Labels; 3.3.1 Error Identification
repro_steps: Open /web/login -> Login as internal user; inspect inputs (no autocomplete), page has no h1 and no main.
expected:
autocomplete="username"/"current-password",

Login

inside
; invalid-credential error linked to the form.
actual: None of these; "Invalid username or password" only via toast/alert region.
user_impact: Password managers and autofill (needed by many cognitive/motor-impaired users, 3.3.8) work less reliably; screen-reader users get no page structure.
root_cause: Props not set.
recommended_fix: Pass autocomplete props; wrap in <main>, use <h1>; render inline form error with role=alert near the submit button.
retest: axe + DOM inspection on /login; Chrome password manager autofill.

wcag_criteria: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; 2.4.6 Headings and Labels

actual: Missing or duplicated.

title: Page titles are not unique across sibling views
evidence: test-results/crawl-results.json: "OpenObserve - Ingestion" x17, "Real User Monitoring" x10, "Databases" x8, "Product Analytics" x7, "Pipeline" x7, plain "OpenObserve" x6

repro_steps: Home: tabs O2 Assistant/Overview/Usage expose role=tab; no element with role=tabpanel exists.
